title: [recoverability] The controllers' drill, LIVE: restore-drill --only controllers checks each controller an active mission's gate names, current and previous, read only, against git archive of its commit from the live source (.controller, .deps, web/node_modules left out); one backup.drilled.controllers per controller; its unit and timer
prompt:
Spawn, objective 198 [recoverability] (the owner's order of 2026-11-14 18:43: restores passed must read 6 of 6, guardrail U1; drill 2 of the owner's four; the lead's acceptance of sync/obj-198/198-proposal.md R2, and the lead's split of 2026-11-15: 198 = LIVE, 199 = BUNDLE->X after it): the controllers' drill, LIVE. What each mission's live system runs from is what its commit says.

A controller is the tree a mission's live system runs from (the gate, its scenarios, the backlog, the maintenance script): `git archive` of one commit of the mission's source under $SPAWN_LIVE/controllers/<name>-<commit>, with <name> and <name>.prev the current one and the one before it (deploy/controller.sh). Nothing checks today that the live tree is still its commit's. 186 proves the mission repositories restore; it does not look at the controllers.

Base: live main b92d1289 (186 landed: `--only missions`, its unit and timer). The throwaway below sits on 186's candidate 00689e69, whose schema, deploy/ and 186.sh are main's byte for byte; main's restore_drill.rs is the fleet's own 186 (only_missions), so the candidate's code is a proof the scenario can be met, not a patch for main.

Read first:
- crates/spawn-cli/src/backup/restore_drill.rs: restore_drill, only_missions (the --only value), drill_parent, drill_record, DrillDir;
- deploy/controller.sh's header (what a controller is, what it adds: .controller, .deps, web/node_modules);
- deploy/systemd/spawn-backup-restore-drill-missions.service (186's unit, which the new unit follows).

What changes:
(1) `spawn backup restore-drill --only controllers` (new module restore_drill/controllers.rs), read only:
   - Which controllers: each open or active mission whose gate lies under $SPAWN_LIVE/controllers/<name>/ (SPAWN_LIVE, else ~/.local/share/spawn-rsi) names controller <name>; its source is the live repository. A mission with a gate elsewhere is skipped and named ("controllers: skipped mission N: ..."). Missions that share a controller but name different sources fail it. Today: spawn (mission 4), supply-pa (6), flake-doctor (9).
   - LIVE, per controller, its current tree and its previous one (when there): the live directory equals `git archive` of its .controller commit from the live source, extracted into scratch. Left out: .controller, .deps and web/node_modules, which deploy/controller.sh adds and git does not hold. Any other path on one side only is a difference. Compared: every file and symlink by path, the executable bit, sha256, and the symlink's target; a file on one side and a symlink on the other differ. Directories are not entries. The live directory is held open while it is read, so a controller switch keeps it (deploy/controller.sh's /proc rule).
   - A controller fails when its live tree differs.
   - One `backup.drilled.controllers` per controller: {type, ok, reason, bundle "", bundle_event_id 0, mismatches, duration_ms, run (the run's start, ms), controller, missions [ids], source, current {commit, live {ok, files, differing [first 20]}}, prev (the same) | null, left_out}. (199 fills bundle and adds held.)
   - Exit 0 only when every controller passed, 1 when one failed or no mission names a controller, 2 when the drill cannot run or a record is refused.
   - `--only` takes missions or controllers; anything else exits 2 with nothing recorded. Without --only the drill is as before.
(2) The schema: spawn_backup_record takes backup.drilled.controllers, with the drill record's fields plus run, controller, missions, source, current, prev and left_out, each checked by kind; nothing else.
(3) The owner's part:
   - deploy/systemd/spawn-backup-restore-drill-controllers.service: `spawn backup restore-drill --only controllers` with the bundle unit's environment and SPAWN_LIVE, Nice 15, idle I/O, MemoryMax 1G, 1 h; exit 1 and 2 not retried.
   - deploy/systemd/spawn-backup-restore-drill-controllers.timer: daily 06:00 (after the 04:00 bundle and 186's 05:45). Installed disabled; enabled after a supervised first run (the owner or the lead).
   - deploy/backup/README.md: the drill, the install steps, and the recovery table's row for U1: {"name": "controllers", "unit": "spawn-backup-restore-drill-controllers.service"}. The unit's result is the run's: "controllers" passed only when every record of the run did (the lead's rule (a)). The row is an owner config change, made after landing.
   - rsi/scenarios/198.sh (new).

Read only, checked before writing this (r198/livecmp.sh, a shell version of the LIVE rule): all six live controllers (spawn 8adefdef/53a3be15, supply-pa a9a06620/384d3597, flake-doctor 58c74c13/d2911fbf) equal their commits, 0 differences over 796/792/1056/1219/112/110 paths.
